resources.string: This only changes the app. It doesn\'t change the system language.

Open an APK, an installed app, or an ELF/.so to inspect ARM64 assembly and control flow. After you pick a function, tap a node to replay from the function entry to that point. This app doesn\'t read private app data and doesn\'t analyze DEX or Java.
Pick an install package and list ARM64 native libraries you can analyze
Browse visible apps, read only public install packages (including splits), then pick a native library
Open a standalone ELF executable or shared library
If the picker hides APKs, browse all files
Try the sample (built-in test file, not a user file)

Only packages the system lets this app see are listed (launcher apps first). A sideloaded build that declares QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES may see more. Store distribution of that permission is restricted, so this is not a complete inventory. Only public sourceDir and splitSourceDirs are read; private data is not.

Only .so files under lib/arm64-v8a and lib/arm64 are listed. Split packages are labeled by source. The whole package is not extracted up front; only the library you pick is. This app does not analyze DEX.
Listed %1$d ARM64 .so files. Choose one. This app does not analyze DEX.
Only public install paths are used. Private app data is not read. Choose an ARM64 .so.
Block instructions come from the icode CFG DOT export. Layout is a local layered layout, not Graphviz.

Select a node or instruction in the graph or listing, then tap Replay. The result is the state after that instruction. Results are read-only.

Results are based on a default execution environment, not values from a real run on the device.

General-purpose registers participate as 0 unless this path writes them. The stack pointer refers to a private stack (address %1$s, size %2$s KiB). The file\'s load segments are mapped. The original file is not written, and no real external functions are called.
